title: Club Governance at a Glance
placeholder: Click any role to see what it is and its single most important responsibility.

nodes.label: Advisory Committee
detail: What it is
An outside group -- a venue host, a school contact, a parent representative -- that reviews the club's direction without running it.
Most important responsibility
Asking the questions nobody inside the club is positioned to ask.
Note
Not every club has one. See the governance structure discussion for when this tier is worth adding.

nodes.label: Club Leader
detail: What it is
The person accountable for the club existing: the venue relationship, the schedule, and the final call on anything contested.
Most important responsibility
Making sure no single decision, including their own departure, can stop the club.

nodes.label: Assistant Leader
detail: What it is
A second person who can run a session end to end without the club leader present.
Most important responsibility
Being genuinely able to substitute -- which requires actually doing it sometimes, not just being named.

nodes.label: Volunteer Coordinator
detail: What it is
The role that owns mentor supply: finding people, getting them screened, and putting them on the calendar.
Most important responsibility
Keeping enough screened mentors scheduled that the club never runs under its ratio.

nodes.label: Mentor
detail: What it is
The screened adult who works directly with students during a session.
Most important responsibility
Being present and attentive to the students in front of them, which is what everything else in this chart exists to enable.

nodes.label: Student
detail: What it is
The person the club is for.
Most important responsibility
Showing up and trying things that do not work at first.

nodes.label: Parent or Guardian
detail: What it is
The adult who consents, transports, and hears about how it went.
Most important responsibility
Knowing enough about what happens in a session to support it at home.
